Subject: Residency question for private deployment (EU primary, APAC standby)

Hi Naomi,

Thanks again for yesterday's demo of the Private deployment option. We're evaluating a configuration where EU is the primary site (data residency requirement) and APAC is a warm standby for disaster recovery. A couple of questions came up from our infra/security team:

- During a failover, can we guarantee no EU-origin data will be routed through APAC systems for more than the RTO window (we need evidence for auditors)?
- How will the VPC peering / BGP handover work if we need to cut over connections — do you have a recommended gating checklist?
- Any example artifacts (network diagrams, routing policy snippets) you can share?

We expect to start a tabletop in two weeks and would like to lock the handshake plan by then.

Appreciate any details and diagrams.

Julie

Julie — thanks, good questions. High level answers first, then I'm looping in Vivek and Karthik for the technical checklist and diagrams.

High level:
- We design the standby so that EU-origin data is not egressed to APAC during normal operation. During a failover, there is a controlled switchover window where replication/handshake happens; our objective is to minimize any transient cross-border traffic and to record an auditable event log for every switchover.
- The winning approach we've used is a two-phase handshake: (1) authorization + read-only synchronization to standby (if needed), (2) controlled route cutover with BGP session adjustments and IP failover. We document the exact TTLs and routing rules for auditors.

Next steps: Vivek will attach a topology diagram and the proposed gating checklist. Karthik will add BGP and routing snippets and the operational runbook steps. I'll consolidate into a single artifact for your tabletop.

Naomi

Julie / team — attaching a topology diagram and a short narrative of the failover phases. See attachments: residency-handshake-diagram.png (visual) and bypass-routing-policy-v1.md (text policy). Highlights below:

1) Failover phases (timeline-based):
   - Phase A: Detection (0s) — primary incident detected, alerts to on-call; no customer routing changes yet.
   - Phase B: Authorization & snapshot (0–90s) — control-plane handshake authorizes failover; select data checkpoints are pushed to standby with encryption-in-transit. We avoid bulk export of EU-resident logs to APAC — only metadata checkpoints are sent unless explicitly authorized.
   - Phase C: Network gating (90–300s) — temporarily withdraw BGP announcements from EU edge for affected prefixes and announce equivalent prefixes from APAC standby; traffic is shifted at the network edge.
   - Phase D: Verification & audit (300–900s) — smoke tests, tokenized verification, and audit log capture confirming all active sessions now originate from APAC prefixes.

2) Key controls to ensure residency compliance:
   - Controlled checkpointing (minimal, encrypted) instead of broad replication unless contractually allowed.
   - Audit event markers stamped with UTC timestamps and failover reason (operator id, justification).
   - Network-level egress filters to block EU-origin data flows to non-EU networks unless whitelisted.

3) Notes on evidence for auditors:
   - We persist time-series of route announcements, API audit events, and signed operator approvals for every switchover. This bundle is exportable as a single compliance artifact.

I've attached the diagram and policy. Olga — can you confirm our default audit retention window and where we stage the export package for customers?

— Vivek
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

Adding concrete routing and ops items — please see inline.

Routing snippets (example):
- EU edge (pre-cutover): announce 198.51.100.0/24 via ISP-A, local-preference 200
- APAC standby (during cutover): announce same prefix via ISP-B with prepended AS-path and local-preference 150; we rely on route communities to prevent internet-sourced traffic from transiting non-authorized backbones.

Gating checklist (operational):
- Confirm operator approval (signed in ticket) — required for any cross-border replication.
- Snapshot verification hash matches primary — no partial states permitted for regulated datasets.
- Disable automatic telemetry egress from EU cluster to external analytics in APAC until post-cutover approval.
- BGP session plan: pre-stage next-hop mappings and test route withdraws in a maintenance window.

Runbook excerpt (for tabletop testing):
1) Trigger detection -> page on-call + open INF-XXXX emergency ticket
2) Run read-only synchronization to cold standby (triggered step, minimal metadata only)
3) Approve operator switch with code phrase and sign-off in ticket
4) Execute BGP withdraws/announces per pre-approved script
5) Run smoke tests and capture audit bundle (route dump, operator signature, timestamps)

Julie — I can be available during your tabletop to run the routing plan. If you'd like, we can do a dry run that only manipulates private peering sessions without touching public announcements.

Thanks,
Karthik
